lines.say: Same deal. Same price. One group showed up almost twice as often.
caps: One group showed up *twice as often.*

lines.say: April, 2004. A car wash. Three hundred customers each got a loyalty card.
The first card had eight empty boxes. The second had ten boxes, but two were already stamped.
Both cards needed exactly eight washes for a free one. Not one wash less.
Nine months later, only nineteen percent of the empty cards ever got finished.
caps: only *19%* of empty cards got finished.

lines.say: The cards with the free head start? Thirty four percent. Almost double.
Two fake stamps. That's it. Two fucking stamps that cost nothing.
People don't finish what they never started. Give a shit about the ones who already did.
Now look at your client list. Half your regulars are cards stuck at stamp three.
Message Health spots who's gone quiet, and texts them before they forget you.
Comment KEEP to get a full retention audit.
